summary: Backend-only testing of 4 new StreamHub features: CloudFront signed-URL settings, subtitle upload (.srt -> WebVTT) with limits/validation/owner-check, public Contact endpoint + admin messages CRUD, and signed subtitle URLs for Pro videos. All 20/20 pytest cases passed (100%). Smoke tests on categories, packages, announcements, admin stats, video listings, and primary+owner admin logins also pass. Settings reset to support@example.com / cloudfront_enabled=false after run.

minor.issue: Accepts untyped dict payload (no Pydantic model). Recommend a typed ContactReq model with EmailStr validation; current code only checks truthiness.
No rate limiting / captcha; public endpoint can be abused to spam contact_messages collection and SMTP.

Extension-only validation (.srt/.ass/.vtt). A file masquerading as .srt with invalid contents will still attempt ffmpeg conversion; fail message returned is generic 500 ('Subtitle conversion failed'). Consider validating content.
Subtitle file size is not bounded server-side; large uploads could exhaust disk.
Returns {ok: true} even when no document matched (idempotent but silent on missing id). Consider 404 for unknown id.

action_items: Add typed Pydantic request model for POST /api/contact (title/message/email with EmailStr).
Add IP-based rate limit and/or captcha on POST /api/contact to prevent spam.
Bound subtitle file size and validate file magic, not just extension.
critical_code_review_comments: storage.py _cloudfront_sign uses SHA1 with PKCS1v15 - this is the correct algorithm CloudFront requires for canned signed URLs, but unit-testing this path was not possible without a real RSA key pair. Code path is structurally correct; if PEM is malformed, presign_get_url silently falls back to S3 presign (good defensive behaviour).
server.py subtitle upload uses shutil.copyfileobj synchronously inside async handler (blocks event loop on large files). Same issue exists in original avatar/cover upload paths.
server.py /api/contact embeds SMTP send inline in the request handler; on slow/failed SMTP this blocks the response up to 15s. Consider a background task / fire-and-forget.
server.py is now ~1255 lines; subtitle + contact endpoints further bloat it. Suggest splitting into routers/{contact,subtitles,videos,admin}.py.
Settings PATCH whitelists keys via AppSettings.model_fields but does not coerce/validate types - e.g. a client could PATCH signed_url_ttl_seconds with a string and break later int(...) casts.

Subtitle URL signing in get_video is good (covers both renditions and subtitles), but the locked-pro branch returns the video with empty renditions yet still includes raw subtitles list - non-Pro users could still see original subtitle URLs in the response. Recommend also clearing/redacting subtitles[] when locked.
/api/admin/contact-messages requires admin (good), but the list is unauthenticated-readable risk only if require_admin is bypassed; verified 403 for non-admin user.
POST /api/contact returns 503 when contact_email is blank - semantically 'service unavailable' is fine, but documenting this status to frontend is important.
test_credentials: admin@streamhub.io / Admin123! (primary), owner@streamhub.io / Owner@2026! (owner) - both verified working
seed_data_creation: Each run creates 2 ephemeral users (test_a_<uuid>, test_b_<uuid>), one TEST_SubVideo (deleted by user via /api/videos), and contact message rows with TEST_ prefixed titles. Contact messages from earlier runs are still visible in admin list (only the test-created one is deleted explicitly).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All four new feature areas verified end-to-end: (1) settings round-trip for contact_email + cloudfront_* fields persists, (2) /api/site/contact-config toggles based on contact_email, (3) /api/contact validates fields + 503 when not configured + admin CRUD works, (4) subtitle .srt is FFmpeg-converted to .vtt (WEBVTT header verified by fetching /api/media/<path>), 10-subtitle limit enforced (11th returns 400), .txt rejected with 400, cross-owner upload returns 403, delete works. Pro-tier subtitle URLs are signed (contain ?exp=&sig= for local storage). Settings reset to support@example.com / cloudfront_enabled=false at end. CloudFront actual signed URL generation could not be E2E-tested without a real key pair, but code path is structurally validated and falls back gracefully on bad PEM.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs blocking the listed features.
